# OpenClaw

OpenClaw is a self-hosted, MIT-licensed gateway that bridges popular chat applications — Discord, Google Chat, iMessage, Matrix, Microsoft Teams, Signal, Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, Zalo, and more — to AI coding agents. A single long-lived Gateway process runs on your own machine or server, acting as the single source of truth for sessions, routing, channel connections, and agent execution. The project targets developers and power users who want a personal, always-available AI assistant they can reach from any messaging app without surrendering data control to a hosted service.

The Gateway exposes a WebSocket control-plane for all clients (CLI, Web Control UI, macOS app, iOS/Android nodes), an optional OpenAI-compatible HTTP surface (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/models`, `/v1/embeddings`), and a built-in scheduler (cron). It embeds a single Pi-agent runtime per process — supporting tool use, persistent memory, multi-agent routing, sandboxing, plugin channels, automation hooks, and custom skills — and can run headlessly as a daemon or interactively via the `openclaw` CLI.

---

## Installation and Initial Setup

Install OpenClaw globally and run the interactive onboarding wizard, which prompts for a model provider API key, configures the Gateway, and optionally installs a background daemon.

```bash
# macOS / Linux — curl installer
curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash

# Windows (PowerShell)
iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1 | iex

# npm (all platforms, Node 24 recommended / Node 22.16+ minimum)
npm install -g openclaw@latest

# Run the interactive onboarding wizard and install system daemon
openclaw onboard --install-daemon

# Verify the Gateway is running (listens on port 18789 by default)
openclaw gateway status

# Open the web Control UI in your browser
openclaw dashboard
```

---

## Gateway Configuration (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`)

OpenClaw reads an optional JSON5 config file at `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`. The Gateway watches the file and hot-reloads changes. Unknown keys or type mismatches cause a hard validation failure and prevent startup. Use `openclaw config get|set|unset` for surgical edits, or edit the file directly.

```json5
// ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json — recommended starter config
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      workspace: "~/.openclaw/workspace",
      model: {
        primary: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6",
        fallbacks: ["anthropic/claude-opus-4-6", "openai/gpt-5.4"],
      },
      models: {
        "anthropic/claude-opus-4-6": { alias: "opus" },
        "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6": { alias: "sonnet" },
        "openai/gpt-5.4": { alias: "gpt" },
      },
      skills: ["github", "weather"],        // shared baseline for all agents
      thinkingDefault: "low",
      timeoutSeconds: 600,
      sandbox: {
        mode: "non-main",                    // sandbox non-main sessions only
        scope: "session",
        docker: {
          image: "openclaw-sandbox:bookworm-slim",
          network: "none",
          readOnlyRoot: true,
        },
      },
    },
    list: [
      {
        id: "main",
        default: true,
        identity: { name: "Clawd", theme: "helpful assistant", emoji: "🦞" },
        groupChat: { mentionPatterns: ["@openclaw", "openclaw"] },
      },
      {
        id: "quick",
        skills: [],                          // no skills — fast, lean agent
        fastModeDefault: true,
        thinkingDefault: "off",
      },
    ],
  },
  channels: {
    whatsapp: {
      dmPolicy: "pairing",                   // pairing | allowlist | open | disabled
      allowFrom: ["+15555550123"],
      groups: { "*": { requireMention: true } },
    },
    telegram: {
      enabled: true,
      botToken: "123:abc",
      dmPolicy: "pairing",
      groups: { "*": { requireMention: true } },
    },
    discord: {
      enabled: true,
      token: "YOUR_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN",
      dm: { enabled: true, allowFrom: ["123456789012345678"] },
      guilds: {
        "123456789012345678": {
          slug: "my-server",
          requireMention: false,
          channels: { general: { allow: true } },
        },
      },
    },
    slack: {
      enabled: true,
      botToken: "xoxb-REPLACE_ME",
      appToken: "xapp-REPLACE_ME",
      channels: { "#general": { allow: true, requireMention: true } },
      dm: { enabled: true, allowFrom: ["U123"] },
    },
  },
  session: {
    dmScope: "per-channel-peer",             // isolate sessions by channel + sender
    reset: { mode: "daily", atHour: 4, idleMinutes: 60 },
    resetTriggers: ["/new", "/reset"],
  },
  messages: {
    visibleReplies: "automatic",
    groupChat: { visibleReplies: "message_tool", historyLimit: 50 },
  },
}
```

---

## CLI Config Commands

One-liner helpers for reading and writing individual config fields without editing the JSON file directly. Changes trigger an automatic hot reload if the Gateway is running.

```bash
# Read a field
openclaw config get agents.defaults.workspace
# => ~/.openclaw/workspace

# Set a scalar value
openclaw config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.every "2h"

# Set a complex JSON value (merge into existing, don't replace)
openclaw config set agents.defaults.models '{"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6":{"alias":"sonnet"}}' \
  --strict-json --merge

# Unset / remove a field
openclaw config unset plugins.entries.brave.config.webSearch.apiKey

# Print the full live JSON Schema for the Control UI and validation
openclaw config schema

# Interactive configuration wizard
openclaw configure

# Full onboarding (provider selection, API keys, daemon install)
openclaw onboard
```

---

## Gateway Lifecycle Commands

The Gateway is the long-lived process that owns channels, agent state, and sessions. All `openclaw gateway` subcommands manage it.

```bash
# Start the Gateway (foreground)
openclaw gateway

# Start as a background daemon (launchd / systemd)
openclaw gateway start --daemon

# Check status
openclaw gateway status

# Graceful restart (picks up config changes and new plugins)
openclaw gateway restart

# Stop
openclaw gateway stop

# Health probe — returns JSON with component statuses
openclaw health
# => {"ok":true,"gateway":{"status":"up","version":"2026.5.9"},...}

# Deep status (sessions, channels, active runs)
openclaw status --deep

# Run diagnostics and auto-repair common issues
openclaw doctor
openclaw doctor --fix
```

---

## Sending Messages and Running the Agent

`openclaw agent` sends a one-shot message to the agent and streams the response. It is the primary non-interactive way to drive the agent from scripts or pipelines.

```bash
# Send a message to the default agent and stream the reply
openclaw agent --message "Summarize the last 10 git commits"

# Send to a specific named agent
openclaw agent --agent quick --message "What is 2+2?"

# Non-interactive with a session key (re-uses context across calls)
openclaw agent --session my-project --message "Now refactor that function"

# Pipe stdin as the message body
echo "Review this diff:" | cat - changes.patch | openclaw agent

# Run with thinking enabled (high / low / off)
openclaw agent --thinking high --message "Architect a multi-tenant SaaS auth system"
```

---

## Multi-Agent Routing

Multiple isolated agents — each with their own workspace, auth profiles, session history, and identity — can run inside a single Gateway. Inbound channel messages are routed via bindings.

```bash
# Add a new isolated agent interactively
openclaw agents add work

# List all agents and their channel bindings
openclaw agents list --bindings

# Switch the default agent
openclaw agents set-default work
```

```json5
// openclaw.json — multi-agent with channel bindings
{
  agents: {
    defaults: { workspace: "~/.openclaw/workspace" },
    list: [
      { id: "personal", default: true, identity: { name: "Clawd", emoji: "🦞" } },
      { id: "work",     identity: { name: "WorkBot", emoji: "💼" } },
    ],
  },
  channels: {
    telegram: {
      enabled: true,
      accounts: {
        personal: { botToken: "111:personal_token", agentId: "personal" },
        work:     { botToken: "222:work_token",     agentId: "work" },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

---

## Session Management

Sessions scope conversation context. By default all DMs share one session; `dmScope` isolates them per sender. Sessions reset on schedule or on `/new` / `/reset` commands.

```json5
// Per-sender isolation + daily reset
{
  session: {
    dmScope: "per-channel-peer",   // per-peer | per-channel-peer | per-account-channel-peer | main
    reset: {
      mode: "daily",               // daily | idle | never
      atHour: 4,                   // reset at 4 AM local time
      idleMinutes: 60,             // or after 60 min of inactivity
    },
    resetTriggers: ["/new", "/reset"],
    maintenance: {
      mode: "warn",
      pruneAfter: "30d",
      maxEntries: 500,
    },
  },
}
```

```bash
# List all sessions
openclaw sessions list

# Show a specific session
openclaw sessions show main

# Delete a session
openclaw sessions delete <sessionKey>
```

---

## Telegram Channel Setup

Telegram is the fastest channel to configure — only a bot token is required.

```bash
# 1. Create a bot in BotFather and get the token.
# 2. Add to config:
openclaw config set channels.telegram.enabled true
openclaw config set channels.telegram.botToken "123456:ABCDEF..."
openclaw config set channels.telegram.dmPolicy "pairing"

# 3. Start / restart the Gateway
openclaw gateway restart

# 4. Approve the first DM pairing request
openclaw pairing list telegram
openclaw pairing approve telegram <CODE>
```

```json5
// Full Telegram config block
{
  channels: {
    telegram: {
      enabled: true,
      botToken: "123456:ABCDEF...",
      dmPolicy: "pairing",          // pairing | allowlist | open | disabled
      allowFrom: ["123456789"],      // for allowlist/open policies
      groupPolicy: "allowlist",
      groupAllowFrom: ["123456789"],
      groups: {
        "-100987654321": { requireMention: true },
        "*": { requireMention: true },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

---

## OpenAI-Compatible HTTP API

The Gateway exposes a drop-in OpenAI Chat Completions surface so any client that expects `/v1/chat/completions` (Open WebUI, LobeChat, LibreChat, etc.) can use OpenClaw as a backend. Disabled by default; enable with one config key.

```json5
// Enable in openclaw.json
{
  gateway: {
    http: {
      endpoints: {
        chatCompletions: { enabled: true },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

```bash
# Chat completions — route to the default agent
curl http://127.0.0.1:18789/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "openclaw",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello from curl!"}],
    "stream": false
  }'

# Route to a specific named agent
curl http://127.0.0.1:18789/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-openclaw-model: anthropic/claude-opus-4-6" \
  -d '{
    "model": "openclaw/work",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Review this PR"}],
    "user": "alice"
  }'
  # `user` field creates a stable session key for multi-turn continuity

# List available agent targets
curl http://127.0.0.1:18789/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN"
# => {"object":"list","data":[{"id":"openclaw"},{"id":"openclaw/default"},{"id":"openclaw/work"}]}
```

---

## Gateway WebSocket Protocol

All control-plane clients connect over WebSocket on port 18789. The first frame must be a `connect` request. After the handshake succeeds the client can send requests and receive streaming events.

```json
// 1. Gateway → Client: pre-connect challenge
{
  "type": "event",
  "event": "connect.challenge",
  "payload": { "nonce": "abc123", "ts": 1737264000000 }
}

// 2. Client → Gateway: connect request
{
  "type": "req",
  "id": "req-1",
  "method": "connect",
  "params": {
    "minProtocol": 3,
    "maxProtocol": 4,
    "client": { "id": "my-client", "version": "1.0.0", "platform": "linux", "mode": "operator" },
    "role": "operator",
    "scopes": ["operator.read", "operator.write"],
    "auth": { "token": "your-gateway-token" }
  }
}

// 3. Gateway → Client: hello-ok
{
  "type": "res",
  "id": "req-1",
  "ok": true,
  "payload": {
    "type": "hello-ok",
    "protocol": 4,
    "server": { "version": "2026.5.9", "connId": "conn-xyz" },
    "features": { "methods": ["agent", "send", "health"], "events": ["agent", "chat", "presence"] },
    "policy": { "maxPayload": 26214400, "tickIntervalMs": 15000 }
  }
}

// 4. Client → Gateway: send an agent turn
{
  "type": "req",
  "id": "req-2",
  "method": "agent",
  "params": {
    "sessionKey": "main",
    "message": "List files in the workspace",
    "agentId": "main"
  }
}

// 5. Gateway → Client: streaming agent events
{ "type": "event", "event": "agent", "payload": { "runId": "run-1", "status": "accepted" } }
{ "type": "event", "event": "agent", "payload": { "runId": "run-1", "delta": "Here are the files..." } }

// 6. Gateway → Client: final response
{ "type": "res", "id": "req-2", "ok": true, "payload": { "runId": "run-1", "status": "done", "summary": "Listed 12 files." } }
```

---

## Scheduled Tasks (Cron)

The Gateway has a built-in scheduler that persists jobs to `~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json` and survives restarts. Jobs can be one-shot, interval-based, or cron-expression-based.

```bash
# One-shot reminder in 20 minutes
openclaw cron add \
  --name "standup-reminder" \
  --at "20m" \
  --session main \
  --system-event "Time for standup — summarize open items" \
  --wake now \
  --delete-after-run

# Recurring job every day at 9 AM Eastern
openclaw cron add \
  --name "morning-brief" \
  --cron "0 9 * * 1-5" \
  --tz "America/New_York" \
  --session main \
  --system-event "Generate morning brief: check calendar, emails, and priorities"

# Fixed interval heartbeat every 30 minutes
openclaw cron add \
  --name "heartbeat" \
  --every "30m" \
  --session main \
  --system-event "HEARTBEAT"

# Inspect jobs
openclaw cron list
openclaw cron get <job-id>
openclaw cron runs --id <job-id>

# Remove a job
openclaw cron remove <job-id>
```

---

## Automation Hooks

Hooks are small TypeScript scripts that fire on Gateway events (`command:new`, `message:received`, `gateway:startup`, etc.). They live in discoverable directories and can push messages back to the user.

```bash
# List available hooks
openclaw hooks list

# Enable a hook
openclaw hooks enable session-memory

# Check hook health
openclaw hooks check
```

```typescript
// ~/.openclaw/hooks/log-inbound/handler.ts
const handler = async (event: any) => {
  if (event.type !== "message" || event.action !== "received") return;

  const { from, content, channelId } = event.context;
  console.log(`[log-inbound] ${channelId} | ${from}: ${content}`);

  // Optionally push a message back to the user
  // event.messages.push("Message logged.");
};

export default handler;
```

```markdown
<!-- ~/.openclaw/hooks/log-inbound/HOOK.md -->
---
name: log-inbound
description: "Log every inbound message to stdout"
metadata:
  { "openclaw": { "emoji": "📝", "events": ["message:received"] } }
---

Logs each inbound message to the Gateway console.
```

---

## Custom Skills

Skills are `SKILL.md` directories that teach the agent when and how to use tools. They follow the [AgentSkills](https://agentskills.io) format and are loaded from the workspace at session start.

```bash
# Create a new skill directory
mkdir -p ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/deploy-check

# Verify the skill loaded
openclaw skills list

# Reload skills without restarting the Gateway
openclaw agent --message "/new"
```

```markdown
<!-- ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/deploy-check/SKILL.md -->
---
name: deploy-check
description: "Run pre-deploy health checks before any production deployment"
---

# Deploy Check Skill

Before any deployment to production:

1. Run `exec("./scripts/health-check.sh")` and confirm exit code 0.
2. Run `exec("git status --short")` and confirm no uncommitted changes.
3. If either check fails, stop and report the failure to the user before proceeding.
```

```bash
# Trigger the skill
openclaw agent --message "Deploy the latest build to production"
```

---

## Plugins

Plugins extend the Gateway with new channels, tools, model providers, and more. They are discovered from [ClawHub](https://clawhub.io), npm, git repos, or local directories.

```bash
# Search for plugins on ClawHub
openclaw plugins search "calendar"

# Install from ClawHub
openclaw plugins install clawhub:openclaw-codex-app-server

# Install from npm
openclaw plugins install npm:@acme/openclaw-plugin

# Install from a local directory
openclaw plugins install ./my-plugin

# List all loaded plugins
openclaw plugins list

# Inspect a plugin's registered tools and services
openclaw plugins inspect openshell --runtime --json

# Enable / disable a plugin (triggers hot reload)
# (run from chat or Control UI)
# /plugins enable openshell
# /plugins disable openshell

# After installing, restart to apply
openclaw gateway restart
```

```json5
// Configure a plugin in openclaw.json
{
  plugins: {
    entries: {
      brave: {
        enabled: true,
        config: {
          webSearch: { apiKey: "${BRAVE_API_KEY}" },
        },
      },
      browser: {
        enabled: true, // bundled browser plugin
      },
    },
  },
}
```

---

## Browser Automation

OpenClaw manages a dedicated, agent-only Chromium/Chrome profile (named `openclaw`) that the agent can control via CDP. This profile is completely isolated from your personal browser.

```bash
# Doctor-check the browser setup
openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw doctor
openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw doctor --deep

# Start the browser
openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw start

# Open a URL in the agent browser
openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw open https://example.com

# Take a snapshot (DOM + screenshot)
openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw snapshot

# Check browser status
openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw status
```

```json5
// Enable in openclaw.json
{
  plugins: {
    entries: {
      browser: { enabled: true },
    },
  },
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      sandbox: {
        browser: {
          enabled: true,
          autoStart: true,
          network: "openclaw-sandbox-browser",
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

---

## Memory System

The agent persists memory as plain Markdown files in the workspace. No hidden state — what is on disk is what the agent knows.

| File | Purpose | When loaded |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `MEMORY.md` | Long-term durable facts and preferences | Every DM session bootstrap |
| `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` | Daily notes, observations, session summaries | Today + yesterday auto-loaded |
| `DREAMS.md` | Dream-diary and dreaming sweep summaries | On demand |

```bash
# Ask the agent to remember something
openclaw agent --message "Remember that I prefer TypeScript over JavaScript"

# Inspect memory files directly
cat ~/.openclaw/workspace/MEMORY.md
ls  ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory/

# Memory vector search (requires embedding model config)
openclaw agent --message "What do you remember about my deployment setup?"
```

```json5
// Enable semantic memory search
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      memorySearch: {
        provider: "gemini",
        model: "gemini-embedding-001",
        remote: { apiKey: "${GEMINI_API_KEY}" },
        extraPaths: ["../team-docs", "/srv/shared-notes"],
      },
    },
  },
}
```

---

## Sandboxing

Tool execution (file read/write, exec, browser) can be sandboxed inside Docker containers or over SSH to limit blast radius.

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      sandbox: {
        mode: "non-main",          // off | non-main | all
        scope: "session",          // agent | session | shared
        backend: "docker",         // docker | ssh | openshell
        workspaceRoot: "~/.openclaw/sandboxes",
        docker: {
          image: "openclaw-sandbox:bookworm-slim",
          workdir: "/workspace",
          readOnlyRoot: true,
          tmpfs: ["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/run"],
          network: "none",
          user: "1000:1000",
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

```bash
# Test sandbox behavior
openclaw sandbox status
openclaw sandbox shell          # open a shell inside the agent's sandbox

# Check elevated (host-escaping) exec policy
openclaw config get tools.elevated
```

---

## Remote Access and SSH Tunneling

The Gateway WebSocket binds to loopback by default. Reach it remotely via SSH port-forwarding or Tailscale.

```bash
# Forward the Gateway port over SSH
ssh -N -L 18789:127.0.0.1:18789 user@myserver.example.com

# With the tunnel active, all local CLI commands target the remote Gateway
openclaw health
openclaw status --deep
openclaw agent --message "What's running on the server?"

# Tailscale Serve — expose the Control UI over your tailnet
tailscale serve --bg 18789

# Multi-gateway: run a second Gateway on a different profile
OPENCLAW_PROFILE=work openclaw gateway --port 18790
```

---

## Model Provider Configuration

Model refs use `provider/model` format. Auth is managed via auth profiles; multiple API keys per provider enable automatic failover.

```bash
# Authenticate a provider interactively
openclaw configure

# Set the primary model
openclaw models set anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6

# List available models
openclaw models list

# Add a provider key as an auth profile
openclaw models auth login --provider anthropic
```

```json5
// Multiple API keys → automatic failover
{
  auth: {
    profiles: {
      "anthropic:default": { provider: "anthropic", mode: "api_key" },
      "anthropic:backup":  { provider: "anthropic", mode: "api_key" },
    },
    order: {
      anthropic: ["anthropic:default", "anthropic:backup"],
    },
  },
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      model: {
        primary: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6",
        fallbacks: ["anthropic/claude-opus-4-6", "openai/gpt-5.4"],
      },
    },
  },
}
```

```bash
# Environment variable API keys (loaded from .env or shell)
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
export GEMINI_API_KEY=...
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...
```

---

## Secrets Management (SecretRef)

Credentials can be stored as SecretRefs (environment variable references or secret-manager paths) instead of plaintext in `openclaw.json`. Resolution is eager at startup; a bad ref on an active surface is a fatal error.

```json5
// Reference secrets from environment variables
{
  channels: {
    telegram: {
      enabled: true,
      botToken: { $env: "TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN" },
    },
    slack: {
      botToken: { $env: "SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" },
      appToken: { $env: "SLACK_APP_TOKEN" },
    },
  },
  gateway: {
    auth: {
      mode: "token",
      token: { $env: "OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN" },
    },
  },
}
```

```bash
# Validate secrets configuration
openclaw doctor

# Rotate a token without restarting — edit config and the Gateway hot-reloads
openclaw config set gateway.auth.token '{"$env":"OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN"}'
```

---

OpenClaw is built for developers who want a personal AI agent reachable from any device, any messaging app, without giving up data ownership. Its single-Gateway design keeps all state — sessions, auth profiles, channel connections, cron schedules, and agent workspaces — in one place under `~/.openclaw/`. The plugin architecture means new capabilities (channels, model providers, tools) arrive as installable packages from ClawHub, while the WebSocket protocol and OpenAI-compatible HTTP surface make it easy to wire OpenClaw into existing tooling. A typical deployment looks like a systemd/launchd daemon on a VPS or home server, with Telegram or WhatsApp as the primary mobile interface and the Web Control UI for desktop management.

Integration patterns range from simple (chat from a phone via Telegram) to complex (multi-agent routing with sandboxed Docker tool execution, vector memory search, cron-driven background research, webhook triggers, and ACP-compatible sub-agent orchestration). The OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint allows drop-in use with frontends like Open WebUI or LobeChat. Custom skills and hooks make OpenClaw extensible without forking: skills teach the model new behavioral patterns via Markdown, hooks react to lifecycle events with TypeScript, and the plugin SDK registers new tools, channels, and providers that hot-reload into a running Gateway.
